items.heading: What their work makes possible.
items.subtitle: The Past, Present and Future of Filmanthropy & Regenerative Filmmaking
items.sourceLabel: Read the full essay on Substack
summary: The film itself is already a gift. This essay follows women who helped filmmaking give in further ways: Mary Pickford helped organize care for film workers; Eva Radke connected production surplus with people who could use it; Vinati and Manjari Makijany helped create a skatepark that remained after filming.

Their stories reveal the practical work behind generosity: building relationships, organizing resources and sustaining what comes next. They also invite us to recognize overlooked pioneers and ask what else the films we make, and the ways we make them, could give.

items.heading: What we become through making.
items.articleTitle: The Irreplaceable Art of Being Human
items.subtitle: AI AND FILMMAKING
summary: Making art changes the people who make it. This essay explores the experience of creating together: rehearsal, vulnerability, trust, discovery and the relationships formed around a shared undertaking. As AI expands what we can generate, Bret asks how the value of those experiences might become more visible, and how the tools could help people collaborate without making the finished output our only measure of the work.

items.heading: Why Filmmaking’s Future Is Human and Civic
items.shareHeadline: Filmmaking as a Human and Civic Act
items.articleTitle: Why Filmmaking’s Future Is Human and Civic
items.subtitle: The original Social Effects NJ note on AI and filmmaking
summary: A film’s value includes the human undertaking that brings it into being: people learning a craft, earning a living, working together and contributing to a place. This original note asks how those gifts might shape filmmaking’s future as AI changes the images we can create.

items.heading: The Giants Who Did It First
items.shareHeadline: A Century of Giving Through Film
items.articleTitle: The Giants Who Did It First
items.subtitle: The Filmanthropy Ledger, No. 1
summary: Giving through film has a history that long predates today’s language of social impact. This essay traces people and precedents from that history, showing how filmmakers have extended their work’s gifts beyond the screen and offering starting points for what productions could make possible next.
